rows.grounds: compound epithet: bhūdhara (earth-holder/mountain) + ānanda (bliss) + ramaṇī (she who delights); feminine nominative singular
compound epithet: bhūdhara (earth-holder/mountain) + ānanda (bliss) + pālinī (she who protects); feminine nominative singular

items.question: How is the goddess characterized through her relation to the bliss of the earth-holder?
premises: The goddess is identified as delighting in the bliss of the earth-holder.
The goddess is identified as protecting the bliss of the earth-holder.
items.inference: The goddess embodies both the enjoyment and the safeguarding of the bliss associated with the earth-holder.
uncertainties: Whether bhūdhara refers specifically to a mountain, the earth, or Śiva as bearer of the earth is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: She delights in the bliss of the earth-holder and protects the bliss of the earth-holder.
